Listen to this article Share …hails him as early champion of ‘democratising luck’ In a rare and emotional display of gratitude in Nigeria’s corporate world, Afrinvest (West Africa) Limited has publicly appreciated billionaire businessman and Chairman of Heirs Holdings, Tony Elumelu, for a personal loan of US$1 million he extended to the company in 2011 at the height of the global financial crisis. In a letter dated October 14, 2026 and signed by its Group Managing Director, Ike Chioke, Afrinvest confirmed that the loan, which was finally settled in June 2026, helped save the firm from collapse and rebuild it into one of Nigeria’s leading diversified financial services groups. According to Chioke, Afrinvest was navigating one of the most challenging periods in its history in 2011 as it struggled to rebuild and recapitalise after the global financial crisis. “At that critical juncture, when the future was far from certain, you made the remarkable decision to lend me US$1 million of your personal funds. You placed your confidence not simply in the prospects of a business, but in me as an individual, my integrity, my determination and my conviction that Afrinvest could emerge stronger from adversity,” Chioke said. He also said that Elumelu’s gesture meant more than he could express at the time, and that today, Afrinvest’s transformation is a vindication of that faith. “From those uncertain days, we have rebuilt and transformed Afrinvest into a diversified financial services group, serving a growing universe of clients and contributing meaningfully to the development of Nigeria’s capital markets. Your faith in me, and in what we were trying to build, has been vindicated,” he said. The Afrinvest boss revealed that when he informed Elumelu in June that he would finally discharge the longstanding obligation, Elumelu was delighted. For Chioke, the repayment was about more than settling a financial debt. “It was about honouring a commitment to someone who believed in me when that belief mattered most. While the financial obligation has now been fully discharged, the debt of gratitude I owe you will endure,” he said. In a striking part of the letter, Chioke linked his personal experience to Elumelu’s famous philosophy through the Tony Elumelu Foundation, “democratising luck”, giving thousands of African entrepreneurs access to capital, mentorship and opportunity. “You understand, perhaps better than most, that talent and ambition are widely distributed, but opportunity is not. By deliberately extending that opportunity to others, you have helped transform individual aspirations into businesses, livelihoods and possibilities that might otherwise never have materialised. “In many respects, I consider myself an early beneficiary of that same philosophy. Long before your Foundation began empowering entrepreneurs across Africa on such an extraordinary scale, you extended a helping hand to me at a defining moment in my entrepreneurial journey,” he said. Chioke described Elumelu’s act as a powerful testament to the multiplier effect of generosity and the enduring value of investing in people. The letter, which has now become public, is being seen in business circles as a powerful lesson in trust, integrity and long-term friendship in an era where business relationships are often transactional. Chioke concluded by saying, “Tony, thank you for believing in me, for standing by me at a difficult time, and for giving me the opportunity to honour that trust. I remain immensely proud of what we have accomplished at Afrinvest, and profoundly grateful that you played such an important part in making it possible.
